messages:
alyssa: spotting a p99 tail on the hosted cluster after last night's runtime deploy. latency spikes ~2x for short-seq requests (<=64 tokens). rolling back didn't change it immediately. digging in now.

alyssa: seems correlated with the new triton kernel selector tweak (prefer_flash=true) we shipped — hoping it's a kernel path mismatch for small sequences. stack: CUDA 535.x, triton 2.44, runtime v3.9.

sre-bot: deploy: runtime/v3.9 rolled at 2026-03-19T01:12:03Z by pipeline #2487.

devin: can you post a quick flame or profile? even a perf counter diff would help.

alyssa: attaching quick nvprof-ish capture from one affected host (redacted):
```
% nvprof --profile-from-start off --print-gpu-trace 
GPU activities:  120.0ms  kernelA (flashAttn_fwd)  40.0%
                90.0ms   kernelB (gemm-based)   30.0%
                60.0ms   kernelC (softmax)       20.0%
Host activities:  <small>memcpy syncs
```
notably some requests are choosing flashAttn_fwd and others fall back to gemm-based but flashAttn runs slower on these hosts for seq<=64 for unknown reason.

mohammed: do we have kernel launch params? shared mem usage etc? flash kernels can regress badly if bank-conflict or occupancy shifts with a new driver.

alyssa: grabbed launch params from kernel tracer: blockDim=(256,1,1) shared=48KB, smem allocated=48KB, occupancy ~0.56 reported. For gemm path blockDim=(128,1,1) shared=32KB.

kevin: there's also that KV-cache alignment change we pushed a couple weeks ago; small-seq requests could be thrashing the cache and changing the effective shape distribution. Any change in batch composition?

alyssa: batch size distribution unchanged by experiment: most short-seq requests single-request batches via continous-batcher. But I did see an uptick in prefix reuse invalidations around the same time — maybe a batching heuristic change triggered more cold cache evictions.

caroline: can you repro locally with the same driver? try forcing kernel selector to prefer_gemm to see if p99 drops back. if so, we can hotfix by toggling selector until we root cause.

alyssa: tried forcing pref_kernel=gemm on one canary node group — p99 dropped ~45% for short-seq. So seems selector led to worse choice on these GPUs.

devin: ok good repro. next: gather per-request kernel choice + sequence length + GPU utilization for a larger sample. also check for noisy neighbor: any tenant that started heavy matrix-mult jobs at that time?

mohammed: I pulled vmstats: noisy VM x10012 had a spike at 01:08Z doing long BERT finetune, but it was pinned to a different GPU slice. However peer PCIe traffic on the host increased ~2x which could affect flash kernels sensitive to PCIe memcpy timing.

kevin: flash kernels often assume low latency copies for KV region updates; if PCIe stalls, their latency can balloon. gemm path maybe more robust to that pattern.

alyssa: also ran a small micro-benchmark: flashAttn_fwd latency vs gemm for seq=32 on the affected host: flash 2.1ms, gemm 1.3ms (flash slower). On a control host: flash 0.9ms, gemm 1.4ms (flash faster). So heterogeneity across hosts.

caroline: that points to driver/hardware interaction. which CUDA driver exactly on repro host vs control?

alyssa: repro host: 535.12.4, control host: 534.98.0.

mohammed: aha — there's been a known regressing commit in 535.x that altered L2 caching behaviour on A100-class GPUs for certain shared-mem patterns. I'll cross-check with vendor notes.

sre-bot: incident: perf-impact-shortseq-2026-03-19 created, severity: medium.

devin: mitigation plan: 1) toggle selector to prefer_gemm for short-seq requests cluster-wide (config gate) 2) roll affected hosts back to 534.x driver or wait vendor patch 3) add a selector heuristic: if flash kernel latency > gemm for same shape on host, prefer gemm.

kevin: I can land a quick runtime override to prefer_gemm for sequence_length<=64 and runtime.config.short_seq_kernel=gemm, canary to 10% first.

alyssa: started canary change at 01:42Z on a small fleet — immediate drop in p99. rolling to 30%.

caroline: longer term: we should add an automated profiling probe that runs small-shape microbenchmarks on each host after driver upgrades and flips selector heuristics if mismatch observed. It'll avoid manual rolls.

mohammed: vendor replied: confirmed they saw a regression in 535.12.x for certain Shared Memory bank patterns and propose a driver patch ETA ~48hrs.

devin: action items: 
- kevin: quick override PR for selector gate (in review)
- alyssa: continue rollout + collect 24hr p99/throughput deltas
- mohammed: validate vendor patch and prepare a candidate driver rollback playbook
- caroline: spec automated microbench probe and follow up with infra on scheduling

alyssa: also: noticed a small increase in KV eviction churn in logs tied to the selector change — will open separate thread to investigate whether kernel path affects eviction heuristics (probably orthogonal but worth tracking).

kevin: PR merged and feature flag on. Kubernetes rollout started at 02:05Z.

sre-bot: deploy: runtime/selector-override rolled at 2026-03-19T02:05:12Z by kevin.

alyssa: rolling to 100% now — p99 for short-seq back to baseline across regions. keeping monitor for 6hrs.

caroline: please add the microbenchmark probe to the infra backlog and schedule driver rollback runbook with ops if vendor patch misses SLA.

mohammed: filing a follow-up to test 535.x with altered kernel launch flags and sharing results.

devin: thanks all — good catch. we'll keep this incident open until vendor patch or driver rollback is done plus the probe is in prod.

alyssa: tl;dr: runtime selector change + driver 535.x interaction caused flashAttn to be chosen on some hosts where it regressed for short sequences -> temporary override to prefer_gemm fixed p99. next steps: probe automation + vendor patch validation. :white_check_mark:
